title: Are these trends connected?
hook: Subtract two known time trends, then inspect the residual relationship.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: any two series that both trend upward correlate strongly; remove the trend and it vanishes.

misconception: Treating two trends as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: any two series that both trend upward correlate strongly; remove the trend and it vanishes.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Two sequences are x=t+[1,−1,0,−1,1] and y=3t+[1,1,−2,1,1], for t=1…5. After subtracting the stipulated trends, what covariance remains?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-two-trends/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Days x=[1,2,3,4,5], y=[3,6,9,12,15] share r=1 solely by the stipulated calendar trend. Subtract each known trend; show residuals [1,-1,0,-1,1] and [1,1,-2,1,1] with covariance zero.

claims.text: The detrended case retains covariance 0; keeping the calendar trends retains covariance 6. Both variables share time structure in this toy model.

claims.text: Subtracting the known trends exposes the residual relationship. In real data the trend is estimated and may be misspecified, so detrending is a model choice rather than proof that all remaining associations are causal.

claims.text: A=2t+u and B=5t+v, with independent zero-mean u and v. What links their raw values? Both include t. Their raw association alone does not orient a causal arrow.
